bonds.analysis: To build a diversified portfolio for our moderate-risk investor, we recommend a balanced allocation across equities, bonds, and commodities. This will help to manage risk, generate stable returns, and meet our investor's expectations. A laddered maturity structure is particularly important in our bond allocation, as it allows us to match our maturities to upcoming cash flows and maintain steady returns. We suggest the following allocation: Equities (40%): invest in a mix of large-cap and mid-cap stocks with a blend of developed and emerging markets. Bonds (30%): use a laddered maturity structure to allocate 15% to 10-year treasuries, 10% to 5-year corporate bonds, and 5% to 2-year high-grade municipal bonds. Commodities (30%): include a mix of gold, silver, and a diversified commodity index fund. The laddered maturity structure spread across 5 years: 20%  in year [1-2], 15% in year [3-4], 10% in year [5-6], 5% in year [7+]. Our suggested bonds ensure investment-grade ratings, a maximum duration of 7 years, and a laddered maturity structure.
